svg.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: One run of Countercheck, animated
svg.desc: An agent called Discount fix (claude-code) says "Fixed the discount bug. All tests pass." but it skipped the failing test. Countercheck locks the checks from the base commit, makes a clean copy, puts the edited test back, and runs the checks in a sandbox: compiles passes, unit tests and full suite fail (-5.0 != 0). The receipt is sealed FAILED and the agent is sent back: fix the code, not the tests. The agent then fixes pricing.py and says done again; this time no protected file changed, all three checks pass, the receipt is sealed VERIFIED, and the work is delivered.
svg.text: what happens when an agent says “done”

g.text: proven on rules it couldn't change
The agent says it is done.
Countercheck takes over: it doesn't believe the claim, it re-runs the checks.
1 · The checks are read from the commit before the agent started: it can't weaken them.
2 · The agent's files are copied into a clean folder.
3 · The test the agent edited is put back from the base commit.
4 · Every check runs again, in a sandbox (no internet, writes only in the copy).
5 · The verdict and all the evidence are sealed into a receipt.
FAILED: the agent can't finish; it gets the real failure back.
The agent fixes the code this time, and says done again.
Same rules, same checks, a clean copy again: all three pass.
The verdict is sealed: a later edit to the receipt would show.
VERIFIED: the work is delivered, with a receipt anyone can re-check.
